note: The third rung set, and the one that asks the question the N=100 rung failed to reach: how does one user's experience change as the crowd grows? Nine levels, C = 1, 5, 10, ... 40, each its own rung with its own cleanup. 40 is the top because SH_SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL defaults to 40 on this deployment and the N=100 rung proved that cap binds: above it, create is refused rather than slowed, so there is nothing to measure. predictions.json (N=10) and predictions-n100.json are not edited.

n100.cause: create refused with quota_exceeded, 'the sandbox service is at capacity', all 60
n100.note: The 40 survivors ran their lifecycle normally: run_id p50 3701 ms against 2219 ms at N=10. But only 40 users ever reached run, so that rung never tested 100-way contention past create.

setting.cluster: OpenShift ykt1, namespace moca-sbx, profile sandbox, control plane main-3b53f15
setting.caps: SH_SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL unset -> code default 40; SH_SANDBOX_MAX_PER_SUBJECT unset -> default 3
setting.driver_host: 18 cores, 64 GB, macOS arm64, over the public Route

predictions.claim: Every level completes with no failure, including C=40, which asks for exactly as many live sandboxes as the cap allows. Each rung deletes its sandboxes before the next begins, and --ladder-settle gives those deletes time to land.

A user's whole lifecycle degrades sub-linearly with the crowd: at C=40 the per-user total p50 is at most twice the uncontended C=1 value. Forty users at once is not forty times the wait, or anything like it.

login is visibly worse under load: at C=40 its p50 is at least 1.3x the C=1 value. The N=100 rung saw 582 -> 1032 ms at 100 concurrent logins against one control-plane pod, so some of that should already show at 40.

run_id degrades more than any other operation between C=1 and C=40. It is the first command in a fresh sandbox and the one that reaches the single sbx-worker replica, so it is where contention should concentrate.
The levels stay mostly concurrent rather than queueing: wall clock at C=40 is at most three times the C=1 wall, against the 40x a sequential run would cost.

The degradation is monotonic in spirit, not merely noisy: the per-user total p50 at C=40 exceeds the one at C=5. If it does not, the ladder has found no contention at all anywhere below the cap, and the only limit on this deployment is SH_SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL.
The driver runs on a free-threaded interpreter at every level.
